display.title: Episode 245: The Secret of the Fireplace (Erev Rosh Hashanah 5747)
display.summary_short: The last show of 5746: a new chapter of The Return of Little Yehudah, the young Tzemach Tzedek hiding in a fireplace to hear the Alter Rebbe teach Torah, and why we blow the shofar.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the last Tuesday of 5746, four days before Rosh Hashanah. Uncle Yossi welcomes the coming year 5747, celebrates five years of Tzivos Hashem on the Air and hopes for the third Beis HaMikdash. After the Hakochainik march, listeners say a prayer for a person who is ill, and a brother and sister lead the Shema. The serial 'The Return of Little Yehudah' continues: escaping the poritz's sand pit, Reb Moshe and Sarah discover that Sarah grabbed the wrong blanket and their baby is still in the pit; Reb Moshe must decide whether to turn back, and the chapter ends there. As an extra treat for the Tzemach Tzedek's birthday on Erev Rosh Hashanah, Uncle Yossi tells how nine-year-old Menachem Mendel, too young for his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's lessons, hid in the empty fireplace to listen, and was found unconscious when a fire was lit until the Alter Rebbe's touch revived him. The show closes with the meaning of the shofar, a wake-up call to teshuvah, and reminders about shofar times and pruzbul.
display.lesson: Love Torah so much that you are ready to give everything to learn more; let the shofar wake you to teshuvah for the new year.

date.note: 'The last Tuesday of this year'; 5747 begins this coming Shabbos (1 Tishrei 5747 = 1986-10-04); Erev Rosh Hashanah is Friday. Weekly estimate was 1986-09-29.

advisories.note: A Jewish couple flees a cruel poritz who held them in a pit; returning would cost their lives.
A baby is left behind in the pit; in the second story a boy is found unconscious in a fireplace when a fire is lit.

privacy.note: Two Shema guests named in full, with ages and school.
A refuah shleimah prayer for a named person (name not captured in the transcript).

sources_cited.note: 'It shall be a day of sounding the shofar for you.'
The shofar as an alarm: 'wake up, sleepers'.
